subject: Andean condor
title: This Bird Flew 100 Miles Without Flapping Once

scenes.text: This giant bird flew over a hundred miles without flapping once.
It's the Andean condor, ten feet across and about thirty-three pounds.
Scientists strapped tags on eight of them and logged over two hundred fifty hours of flight.
Only about one percent of that time was flapping, and three quarters of that was takeoff.
The secret is invisible. Warm air rises off the Patagonian mountains, and they ride it for hours.
One bird stayed up five hours without a single flap. The wing does nothing. The sky does the work.

description:
This giant bird flew over a hundred miles without flapping once.
Tagged Andean condors flapped for only about one percent of their flight time, riding rising warm air for hours.
Would you trust the wind that much?
first_comment: A condor spends about one percent of its flight flapping. What's the laziest animal trick you know?
